concerns.text: T015B is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T014A checking for `data/raw/am_data.csv`. If T014A fails (file missing), T015B cannot execute its logic. Parallel tasks must not have implicit runtime dependencies on the success/failure of sibling tasks. T015B should be sequential after T014A.

T016 depends on T015B producing `data/processed/excluded_columns.yaml`. However, T015B is marked [P] and listed in a parallel block with T014A. If T015B runs in parallel with T014A, the file may not exist when T016 starts. T015B must be sequential after T014A, and T016 must wait for T015B.

T031 depends on T029A (metrics.json) and T026 (GPR model). The description states T031 'Appends results to results/metrics.json'. T029A also writes to `results/metrics.json`. If T031 runs in parallel with any other task writing to this file (or if T029A is not strictly finished), race conditions occur. T031 must be strictly sequential after T029A completes.

T043 (E2E) depends on T031. The description says 'T031 is NOT a prerequisite dependency for T043 to start'. This contradicts the explicit `[DEPENDS ON ... T031]` tag in the task header. If T043 starts before T031, it will fail to find the appended importance correlation data in `metrics.json`.

T019 saves `normalization_bounds.json`. T038 depends on T019. T019 is not explicitly marked as a dependency for T035/T036 in the header, but T038 depends on T035/T036. The flow is T016 -> T019 -> T038. Ensure T019 is listed as a dependency for T038 explicitly in the header to avoid ambiguity.
